newsitem.title: UK: UK minister welcomes drop in claimant count.
newsitem.headline: UK minister welcomes drop in claimant count.

text.p: UK education and employment minister Andrew Smith welcomed an 18,400 fall in claimant unemployment in May, which he said was consistent with a broad picture of rising growth and employment.

"These figures are the first unaffected by distortions to the claimant count caused by the introduction of the Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA). We shall, however, need to get a run of figures and additional evidence from the Labour Force Survey (LFS) before a firm picture of the labour market can be established," he said in a statement.
"The figures are, however, consistent with a broad picture of rising output, growth in employment and falling unemployment."

Other figures indicated that the labour market was improving: employment rose 86,000 in the quarter to March and 359,000 on the year; new vacancies were still being reported to Jobcentres at a high level, 239,000 in May; and fewer people were being made redundant.
The Department for Education and Employment said earnings growth remained low by historical standards although it had risen since its trough.
"Earnings growth is at low levels and there are few signs of bottlenecks in the labour market," it said.
